stories.title: Forthcoming briefing paper on offences of failing to disclose information – Law Commission
stories.source_name: Law Commission of England and Wales

seen_in.source_name: Law Commission of England and Wales

stories.ltme_summary: The Law Commission says it is preparing a briefing paper on offences of failing to disclose information, responding to recommendation 67 of the Southport Public Inquiry's first report. The paper will set out existing law and the section 38B Terrorism Act 2000 comparison, but will make no reform proposals. It expects publication before the end of 2026.
stories.hook: Law Commission to publish Southport duty-to-report briefing before end of 2026

Why law firms need spaces for ethical reflection
stories.ltme_summary: A solicitor researcher argues in Solicitors Journal that law firms should hold regular structured sessions on ethical dilemmas, which the author calls solicitors' sharing spaces. The piece draws on 88 survey responses and 30 interviews from doctoral research on professional integrity. It recommends monthly sessions facilitated by a partner or compliance officer.
stories.hook: Solicitor researcher urges monthly ethics sessions in every firm

In-House And AI: You Can’t Demand What You Don’t Understand
stories.ltme_summary: A US commentator writes on Legal Tech Monitor that in-house counsel do not demand that outside lawyers use AI to cut fees. The author draws on a recent Axiom study to argue in-house teams do not understand AI well enough to know what to ask for. The piece links to a longer post for Above the Law.
stories.hook: Commentary argues in-house counsel cannot demand AI they do not understand

stories.hook: Illinois Supreme Court creates standing committee to study AI risks
entities: Supreme Court Committee on Artificial Intelligence

stories.title: Speech by Sir Colin Birss, Master of the Rolls: AI and Legal Reasoning
stories.ltme_summary: Sir Colin Birss, Master of the Rolls, delivered the James Wood public lecture at Glasgow University on 20 November 2026. He examines the capabilities of AI and its use in law, focusing on civil justice in England and Wales, and how AI relates to legal reasoning. The extract covers the opening sections on the development of language models.
stories.hook: Master of the Rolls sets out his view of AI and legal reasoning

stories.title: US in-house moves: Legora hires first ever CLO as Fox and Dell pick up new legal chiefs
stories.ltme_summary: Legora has hired Erika Fisher as its first chief legal officer, moving from HubSpot, where she was chief legal officer for nearly two years. The Legal Business round-up also covers in-house moves at Fox and Dell. The extract shows the Legora appointment as the lead item.
stories.hook: Legora appoints Erika Fisher as first chief legal officer

stories.title: Former Perkins Coie London head Bagshaw leads four-lawyer team to King & Spalding
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that King & Spalding is set to hire Ian Bagshaw, former head of Perkins Coie's London office, with a four-lawyer team. The move is reported as based on what Legal Business understands. King & Spalding's London business has grown, according to the extract's related reporting.
stories.hook: King & Spalding set to hire former Perkins Coie London head Ian Bagshaw

stories.title: ‘This is only the start’ – Morgan Lewis breaks down its continental buildout
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that Morgan Lewis is pursuing a more integrated European business to compete in cross-border deals. Munich managing partner Florian Harder says the EU platform matters to its M&A and private equity clients, citing investment from the US and the Middle East. The extract is the article opening.
stories.hook: Morgan Lewis bets on integrated European platform for cross-border deals

stories.title: Sidley swoops for 25 lawyers from Weil’s London office
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that Sidley is set to welcome a 25-strong team from Weil's London office, including former London managing partner Jonathan Wood and private equity co-head Marco Compagnoni. Sidley says London headcount has grown 50 per cent over two years. Weil is winding down after more than 90 years.
stories.hook: Sidley takes 25 lawyers from winding-down Weil London office

stories.title: City-backed SQE fund for aspiring social welfare lawyers tops £2 million
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that the Social Welfare Solicitors' Qualification Fund has secured more than £2 million in pledges, enough to support 175 aspiring social welfare solicitors. The City of London Law Society launched the scheme in 2021 with BARBRI. Sarah Sackman KC MP welcomed the milestone.
stories.hook: Social welfare solicitor fund passes £2m in pledges from City firms

stories.title: Macfarlanes selects Legora as a firm-wide AI partner
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider reports that Macfarlanes has selected Legora as a firm-wide AI partner. The extract is limited to a verification page, so the details rest on the headline alone and the outlet's own text is not visible to us. Macfarlanes is a London firm already associated with another legal AI platform in other coverage.
stories.hook: Macfarlanes picks Legora as a firm-wide AI partner

stories.title: From tasks to matters: New benchmark tests the limits of frontier AI
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider reports on a new benchmark that tests frontier AI models on legal matters rather than discrete tasks. The extract is a bot-check page, so the benchmark's authors, scoring and results are not visible in what we hold.
stories.hook: New benchmark moves frontier AI testing from tasks to matters

stories.title: Early Harvey adopter Macfarlanes adds rival Legora
stories.ltme_summary: Nonbillable reports that Macfarlanes has announced a firm-wide partnership with Legora while keeping Harvey available across the firm. A firm spokesperson says the firm will use the right tools for each task. Legora's legal engineers are building bespoke Skills with the firm, with more detail due in January.
stories.hook: Macfarlanes adds Legora alongside Harvey in firm-wide multi-platform approach

stories.title: King & Spalding hires Ian Bagshaw in four-lawyer London move from Ashurst Perkins Coie
stories.ltme_summary: Nonbillable reports that King & Spalding has hired Ian Bagshaw from Ashurst Perkins Coie in a four-lawyer London move, including Craig Fagan and two counsel. Bagshaw says he is leaving the firm, which combined with Perkins Coie on 29 June this year. The article says King & Spalding declined to comment.
stories.hook: King & Spalding hires Ian Bagshaw from Ashurst Perkins Coie

stories.title: Conviction for publishing mediation discussions was not rights violation
stories.ltme_summary: The European Court of Human Rights has ruled there was no breach of Article 10 when Belgian journalist Françoise de Halleux was convicted over publishing a mediation meeting she overheard. Fines of €3,000 for her and €21,000 for Sudmedia were upheld as proportionate. The case concerned the Dutroux affair mediation.
stories.hook: ECtHR upholds conviction of journalist over published mediation account

stories.title: Insurers told to brace for credit hire costs rise in 2027
stories.ltme_summary: QG Law's Gary Herring predicts credit hire costs per claim will rise by an average 19 per cent next year for claims outside the General Terms of Agreement. Costs under the GTA could rise about 11 per cent between 2027 and 2029. The forecast cites longer repair times and EV claims costing a quarter more.
stories.hook: QG Law forecasts credit hire costs up 19 per cent for non-GTA claims in 2027

stories.title: SRA marks its territory as NDA ban moves up the agenda
stories.ltme_summary: The SRA has reaffirmed its position on solicitors abusing their power in response to the prime minister's pledge to restrict non-disclosure agreements. The regulator's chief executive, Sarah Rapson, says misuse of litigation and improper NDAs fall below expected standards. The government says NDAs will no longer gag employees from January. A private member's SLAPP bill is due in the Commons.
stories.hook: SRA reaffirms NDA stance as government moves to curb gagging clauses

stories.title: BSB chief agrees ban for antisemitic posts 'apparently lenient'
stories.ltme_summary: The Bar Standards Board says it will consider further action after an independent tribunal suspended barrister Forz Khan for four months over antisemitic LinkedIn posts. Shadow ministers had criticised the sanction as lenient. BSB chair Professor Chris Bones says the regulator needs the written tribunal reasons before deciding. Khan was also ordered to pay £2,880 costs.
stories.hook: BSB to review four-month suspension of barrister over antisemitic posts

Form: Order for recovery of unpaid penalty charge: Form TE3
stories.ltme_summary: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has published form TE3, the order for recovery of unpaid penalty charge. A minor amendment to the first bullet point on page one was made on 26 November 2026, following an updated version dated 1 October 2026.
stories.hook: HMCTS amends form TE3 for recovering unpaid penalty charges

stories.title: Interest rate increased on the Court Funds Office special and basic accounts: November 2026
stories.ltme_summary: The Ministry of Justice says interest rates on Court Funds Office special and basic accounts rise from 26 November 2026, following the Bank of England base rate increase on 5 November. The special account moves from 3.75 per cent to 4.00 per cent and the basic account from 2.81 per cent to 3.00 per cent.
stories.hook: Court Funds Office raises special and basic account rates from 26 November

stories.title: Pink Larkin names Jill Houlihan as its new managing partner as of 2027
stories.ltme_summary: Pink Larkin has named Halifax-based partner Jillian Houlihan as its managing partner from 1 January 2027, according to the firm's news release. She succeeds Ron Pink, the firm's inaugural managing partner, who has held the post for more than 35 years. Houlihan will keep practising from the Halifax office. Joël Michaud, a member of the management committee, comments on her appointment.
stories.hook: Pink Larkin names Jillian Houlihan as managing partner from January 2027, succeeding founding leader Ron Pink

stories.title: BC law society adds diversity questionnaire on demographics
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society of British Columbia has opened a voluntary demographic questionnaire covering 10 characteristics, available to members after they complete their mandatory annual practice declaration from 23 November. According to the society's news release, only lawyers who have finished the declaration are being asked this year. The data will feed policy on access and retention, and the society says it will not use the answers in regulatory processes.
stories.hook: Law Society of British Columbia opens voluntary demographic questionnaire to members after annual practice declaration

stories.title: ‘We do need to change things’ – Pinsents’ new leaders on returning the firm to its innovation roots
stories.ltme_summary: Pinsent Masons' new managing partner Richard Griffiths says it is healthy for the firm's elections to be contested. Griffiths took up the role on 1 November, working alongside senior partner John Maciver, who also won a contested election. They replace Laura Cameron and Andrew Masraf. The piece frames the leaders' plans around returning the firm to its innovation roots.
stories.hook: Pinsent Masons' new managing partner Richard Griffiths says the firm must change after contested leadership elections

7 Best Legal Outsourcing Companies in 2027: Costs, Services and Expertise Compared
stories.ltme_summary: LawFuel carries a sponsored-style ranking of seven legal outsourcing companies for 2027, written by HireParalegals' head of growth. It names HireParalegals best overall and compares hourly rates, with pricing drawn from provider information as of November 2026. The article uses BLS salary figures to argue that outsourcing can cut staffing costs for small and midsized US firms.
stories.hook: HireParalegals promotes its own ranking of legal outsourcing firms, claiming savings of up to 81 per cent on staffing costs

AI in law firms: what supervising AI-assisted work actually involves
stories.ltme_summary: Rafael Patron, president of the scientific-technical committee of the Italian Association of Artificial Intelligence Professionals, argues in a guest post that supervising AI-assisted legal work needs more than citation checks. He proposes sorting AI-assisted tasks by the consequences of an error rather than by tool used. He cites the SRA's warning notice on AI misuse published on 17 August and recent hallucination tracker counts.
stories.hook: Citation checks catch only the crudest AI failures, according to a guest post on supervising AI-assisted legal work

stories.title: AI-native startup looking to “redesign how a law firm works”
stories.ltme_summary: Kyra Law, an AI-native commercial startup, says it has taken over 150 clients in its first six months, mostly startups and scaleups, and has more than £1m of annualised revenue. Co-founder Joey Irwin told Legal Futures the firm uses AI to run its administration, including onboarding, billing and KYC checks, and offers fixed fees. The firm is not currently regulated and is self-funded. Three further solicitors are set to join.
stories.hook: Kyra Law says AI handles much of its firm administration as it passes 150 clients with fixed fees and no regulation

stories.title: Law firm launches service to tackle mistranslation
stories.hook: Inksters launches Translation Law to help lawyers handle errors in AI and human translations of legal documents

EVOX, a maker of stock car images, alleges unlicensed uses of its images and uses beyond a 2020 licence. The post links to Google's motion to dismiss, and the commentator calls the dispute fascinating.
stories.hook: Google seeks to dismiss three of five claims in EVOX Productions' amended copyright complaint

stories.title: News Plaintiffs file their summary judgment motion on RAG and outputs v. OpenAI
stories.source_name: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.ltme_summary: The News Plaintiffs have filed a summary judgment motion against OpenAI on outputs and retrieval-augmented generation, according to Edward Lee's tracker. The motion is heavily redacted in the public version, which the commentator says will make much of it hard to follow. The filing is part of the wider AI copyright litigation against OpenAI.
stories.hook: News Plaintiffs seek summary judgment against OpenAI on outputs and RAG, with the filing heavily redacted

stories.title: The Cyber Security and Resilience Bill: What the construction industry needs to know
stories.ltme_summary: Trowers & Hamlins outlines the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill for construction and infrastructure firms. The Bill extends the NIS Regulations to managed service providers, large data centres and critical suppliers, with two-stage incident reporting within 24 and 72 hours. Penalties would reach £17m or 4 per cent of worldwide turnover for serious breaches. The Bill is in its final stages before Royal Assent.
stories.hook: Cyber Security and Resilience Bill would bring managed service providers and data centres into NIS scope, says Trowers

stories.title: Amended pre-action protocol for housing conditions claims
stories.ltme_summary: Trowers & Hamlins summarises the amended pre-action protocol for housing conditions claims in England. The revised protocol makes ADR an explicit objective, allows the court to order ADR, and drops compliance where urgent health and safety or statutory deadlines apply. It shifts focus towards hazards under Awaab's Law and the 2025 Regulations.
stories.hook: Amended housing conditions protocol makes ADR central and brings Awaab's Law hazards into claims, says Trowers
entities: Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025

stories.title: Trowers Tuesday: Mastering employment tribunals - Turning pressure into advantage: putting…
stories.ltme_summary: Trowers & Hamlins promotes a webinar on Tuesday 1 December in its employment tribunals series, covering how AI can support employers with grievances, disciplinaries and tribunal claims. Speakers will discuss legal privilege when using AI tools and safeguards for adopting new technology. The page also contains standard webinar data protection notices.
stories.hook: Trowers & Hamlins webinar asks how employers can use AI in grievances and tribunal claims without losing privilege

stories.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Workplace: Italy strengthens human oversight
stories.ltme_summary: Watson Farley & Williams reports that Italian Legislative Decree No. 179/2026 entered into force on 23 October 2026, strengthening human oversight of AI used in employment relationships. The extract is a single summary line, so the detailed obligations are not visible from it.
stories.hook: Italy's Legislative Decree 179/2026 on AI in the workplace took effect on 23 October 2026, says WFW

Mishcon de Reya revenues rise to £372 million with profits of £127 million for 2025/26
stories.ltme_summary: Mishcon de Reya has reported revenue of £372m for its last financial year, up 13 per cent, with profit rising 15 per cent to £127m. The firm describes this as continued robust growth and expansion. The figures come from the firm's own announcement.
stories.hook: Mishcon de Reya reports revenue up 13 per cent to £372m and profit of £127m for 2025/26

stories.title: Implementation timeline accelerated for restrictions on NDAs about discrimination and harassment
stories.ltme_summary: Mishcon de Reya says the Employment Rights Act 2025 makes non-disclosure agreements void where they stop workers making allegations or disclosures about harassment or discrimination. The firm reports the implementation timeline has been accelerated. The extract is a single summary line, so the date and the new commencement timing are not clear from it.
stories.hook: Mishcon de Reya reports accelerated timetable for banning NDAs that gag harassment and discrimination complaints

stories.title: Dentons Rodyk appoints Edric Pan as Managing Partner
stories.hook: Edric Pan takes over as Dentons Rodyk managing partner from 1 January 2027, also taking the Dentons ASEAN CEO role

stories.title: LSBC readies AML/CTF risk assessment tools for profession
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society of British Columbia has prepared firm-level and client-level anti-money laundering risk assessment tools for lawyers, responding to concerns in the Financial Action Task Force's 2026 Mutual Evaluation Report of Canada. The society says the Federation of Law Societies of Canada is considering requiring some risk assessments. The FATF had called law society sanctions ineffective and too lenient, and noted gaps on politically exposed persons.
stories.hook: LSBC readies AML risk assessment tools after FATF criticised Canadian law society sanctions as too lenient
entities: Federation of Law Societies of Canada

Charitable gifts now in nearly 30% of wills as advisers expect IHT shifts to fuel legacy giving
Farewill marks 10th anniversary with £1.6bn of legacy donations
Strategic succession and knowing your worth in estate planning
The real reason legal tech falls short
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp, a vendor of law firm software, publishes five practices it says separate firms that get results from AI and technology investments. The advice includes setting business outcomes before features, treating vendor proposals as multi-year roadmaps, funding change management and building AI governance from the start. The piece is written by Intapp's Legal Strategic Advisory team and promotes its Intapp Celeste offering.
stories.hook: Intapp argues law firms fail with technology because they buy features rather than set business outcomes

stories.title: Building sustainable legal careers in the age of AI: a practical perspective from the front line
stories.ltme_summary: Osprey Approach has published a podcast interview from its Empowering Law Firm Leaders series, episode 39, with Helen Barry, Director and Head of Property at Watkins & Gunn Solicitors. She discusses alternative routes into law, sustainable legal careers, training juniors when AI takes over routine tasks, and AI in conveyancing. The content is a vendor-hosted interview rather than news.
stories.hook: Watkins & Gunn's Helen Barry urges firms to make alternative qualification routes visible as AI changes junior work
